title: Generic generator lifting on an irreducible constant base
statement: Let X be an irreducible scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions] with generic point eta [def-sc-generic-point], and Lambda a Noetherian commutative ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Let phi:F to G be a monomorphism of Lambda-module sheaves on its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Assume G is constant [def-constructible-constant] and finite (its geometric stalks [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks] are finitely generated). There is an open U containing eta, a finite locally constant sheaf H on U [def-constructible-finite-locally-constant], and a monomorphism H to the pullback of F to U which is epi at every geometric point over eta. No Noetherianity of X, finiteness of the underlying set of Lambda or G, or equality of H and F away from eta is asserted.

source.place: Tag 09BH, Proposition 59.74.1 (3), generator lifting and descent on the irreducible constant base, before the final equality

proof.text: Choose a constant value M of G. A geometric generic stalk is M, so M is finitely generated. The monomorphism identifies the generic stalk of F with a submodule N of M. Since Lambda is Noetherian, N is finitely generated.

Choose generators of N and represent them on one common pointed etale neighbourhood. Refine until their images equal the corresponding constant sections of M; equality in the filtered-colimit stalk holds after refinement. On the fibre product their two pullbacks agree, because their images in constant M agree and phi is mono. Descend the lifts to the open image U of this neighbourhood, which contains eta.

Every linear relation in N vanishes after mapping to M and hence already in F by monicity. The lifted sections thus give a morphism from the constant sheaf N to F on U. Its composite into constant M is the constant inclusion, which is mono since the constant-presheaf functor and sheafification preserve monos. Hence the morphism into F is mono. Set H equal to this constant N sheaf: finite generation of N gives finite local constancy.

The chosen generic stalk map is surjective because its image contains the generators of N. Generic stalks for arbitrary separably closed extensions of the residue field are identified after choosing compatible separable closures, with the same images in constant M. Therefore this surjectivity holds for every geometric point over eta. For N=0 use the zero constant sheaf; no equality of H and F away from the generic point is required.
